paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in Judges 9. Abimelech wanted a crown so badly that he grabbed it by the worst road there is. He pitched the leaders of Shechem on his own family tie, and they said, "He is our brother." Their hearts leaned his way because of that tie (Judges 9:2-3).

Now look at Jotham's story about the trees. The olive tree, the fig tree and the grapevine each had something good to give, and each one stayed busy giving it (Judges 9:9, 11, 13). The only one who said yes to the crown was the thornbush, and its first move was a threat about fire (Judges 9:15). I think Jotham is showing us that the ones who are eager to rule aren't always the ones worth following.

So here's what I'm taking home, baker. Before you follow somebody, ask what they're after, and don't stop at who they're related to or how smooth the pitch was. Ask the same about yourself, because that crown can sneak into any heart. Jotham asked the leaders if they had acted "faithfully and honestly" (Judges 9:19), and that is a question worth asking before every big decision.
